items.followUp: Give another example of a Boolean proposition and state whether it is true or false.

rubric.why: An example of a proposition is required.
rubric.description: Gives a statement that can be judged true or false.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a valid example of a Boolean proposition.

rubric.why: A proposition has a definite truth value.
rubric.description: States the truth value of the example.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly identifying the example as true.

modelAnswer: “2 is an even number” is a Boolean proposition.
It has the truth value True.

rubric.description: Identifies the act as illegal or unauthorized.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that the act is illegal or unauthorized.

rubric.why: The definition must identify what is being pirated.
rubric.description: Mentions copying, using, or distributing software without permission.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying unauthorized copying, use, or distribution of software.

modelAnswer: Software piracy is the illegal or unauthorized copying, use, or distribution of software.
It violates the software owner's copyright.

items.followUp: What happens to an operating system when a computer is started from its hard disk?

rubric.why: The answer should identify the source of the operating system during startup.
rubric.description: States that the operating system is loaded from the hard disk.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming the hard disk as the source.

rubric.why: The answer should identify where the operating system is loaded for use.
rubric.description: States that the operating system is loaded into RAM (main memory).
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming RAM or main memory as the destination.

modelAnswer: During hard-disk loading, the operating system is read from the hard disk.
It is loaded into RAM so that the computer can use it.

items.followUp: What is meant by a communication medium?

rubric.why: A communication channel is the route or medium used for communication.
rubric.description: Identifies the channel as a medium, path, or means.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying it as a medium, path, or means.

rubric.why: The channel connects the communicating parties.
rubric.description: States that it carries data or messages from sender to receiver.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that it carries communication from sender to receiver.

modelAnswer: A communication channel is the medium or path used to transmit data.
It carries a message from the sender to the receiver.

items.followUp: How can two computers on a network share a file?

rubric.why: The answer should describe the activity involved.
rubric.description: Identifies file sharing as making a file available to others.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining that a file is made available or shared.

rubric.why: File sharing commonly allows users or computers to exchange files over a network.
rubric.description: Mentions sharing or transferring files between users or computers over a network.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning users or computers and a network.

modelAnswer: File sharing is the process of making files available to other users or computers.
The files can be exchanged over a network.

items.followUp: Name two components of a communication system and state their roles.

rubric.why: Sender and receiver are essential components of communication.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming both the sender and the receiver.

rubric.why: A communication system also includes what is sent and how it is transmitted.
rubric.description: Names the message and a communication channel or medium (or protocol).
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming the message and at least one of channel, medium, or protocol.

modelAnswer: The components of a communication system include the sender and the receiver.
They also include the message, the communication channel or medium, and the protocol.

items.followUp: What is the difference between a message and a communication channel?

rubric.why: A message is the content being communicated.
rubric.description: Defines a message as data or information.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the message as data or information.

rubric.why: The definition should show the direction or purpose of the message.
rubric.description: States that the message is sent from a sender to a receiver.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming the sender and receiver.

modelAnswer: A message is the data or information that is communicated.
It is sent by a sender to a receiver.

items.followUp: Write a short HTML example of a list containing a nested list.

rubric.why: The defining feature of a nested list is that one list is placed inside another.
rubric.description: States that a list is placed inside another list.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining the list-within-a-list structure.

rubric.why: A nested list is used to show subordinate items under a main item.
rubric.description: Explains that it represents subitems or items under a main list item.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing its use for subitems or subordinate items.

modelAnswer: A nested list is a list placed inside another list.
It is used to show subitems under a main list item.
